title: Set up two Meshtastic radios for the family
summary: Step by step: flash, pair, set the region, name your radios, create a private channel, share it by QR code, and test.

sources.title: Meshtastic: nRF52 drag and drop updates

blocks.text: This walks through setting up **two Meshtastic radios** so family members can text each other with no cell service. Do it all **now**, with internet, then test outdoors. A radio is useless in an outage if it was never set up.
**Attach the antenna before you power on any radio.** The Meshtastic docs say powering on without one could damage the radio chip.

You will need two radios, a USB cable that carries data (not only charge), and a phone for each radio. A radio pairs with one phone at a time, and the docs list apps for Android and Apple. Phones need Bluetooth on.

items: **Test the cable.** Copy a file to or from a phone over it. A charge-only cable will not work.

**Put the software on the radio (a computer and internet needed).** For most boards: open flasher.meshtastic.org in **Chrome or Edge**, plug in the radio, and follow the on-screen instructions. Some radios (nRF52, RP2040) update by drag and drop instead: double-press the reset button, a drive appears, and you copy the matching .uf2 firmware file onto it. Use the file made for your exact board. Wrong firmware can leave the radio with a blank screen.
**Install the Meshtastic app** on the phone and turn Bluetooth on.

**Pair.** Android: open the **Connect** tab, tap **Scan for Bluetooth devices**, pick your radio, and enter the PIN. If the radio has a screen, type the six-digit PIN it shows. A radio with no screen uses 123456. Android needs the **Nearby devices** permission. iPhone: open the **Connect** tab and tap the radio's name. Radios with a color touchscreen ship with Bluetooth off; turn it on from the radio's menu first.
**Change the default PIN** if your radio uses the fixed one. The docs warn that leaving 123456 is a security risk. In Bluetooth settings, choose a fixed PIN and enter your own six digits.

**Set the region to US.** Android: **Settings > LoRa > Region**, then Save (or tap SET YOUR REGION on the device card). iPhone: **Settings > Radio Configuration > LoRa**. Without a region the radio will not transmit.
**Check the preset.** Make it **LongFast** on both radios. A US radio whose region was set from its own screen may start on LongTurbo, and the two will not hear each other.
**Set a name.** Android: **Settings > User**. The Long Name can be up to 39 characters and the Short Name is a 4-character abbreviation. Save. Use a name the family will recognize, such as initials.

**Create the private channel.** Android: **Settings > Channels**, tap **+**, enter a channel name, and let the app generate the 256-bit key. Tap **Save**, then tap **Send** to write it to the radio. If you skip Send, the change stays only on the phone. iPhone: **Radio Configuration > Channels**. Add it as a secondary channel and leave the primary channel at its default.

**Share it by QR code.** Open the channel's share screen on the first phone, then scan the code with the second phone (Android: the in-app scanner; iPhone: the camera). The scan copies the channel and radio settings. Print the QR code and keep it in the go-bag.

**Send a test message.** Use a **direct message** to the other person, not the channel. Only a reply from the other radio confirms delivery. A channel message can look delivered when only one nearby radio repeated it.
**Walk apart and test.** Take the radios outside and increase the distance until messages stop. Note how far that is for your neighborhood.
**Position (optional).** Open the Position settings in the app. A radio with GPS can share its location. You can instead enter a **fixed position** that the radio reports in place of live GPS.
**Save your settings.** Android: **Settings > Backup & Restore > Export configuration** saves a file. Do this before any factory reset.
Antenna attached to each radio
Region set to US on both radios
Preset set to LongFast on both radios
Both radios on the same private channel (same name and key)
Names set so you know who is who (note them on the Comms screen under Mesh)
Default Bluetooth PIN changed
Test direct message sent and answered
Walked apart and noted the distance where messages stop
Radios charged, and the cable and charger in the go-bag
QR code printed, configuration exported
Phone app installed and Bluetooth tested on every phone that will use it

blocks.text: If the troubleshooter on the Comms screen (Mesh > Troubleshoot) does not fix a problem, fall back to the next method in your family PACE plan.
